description:
Phase 6. Healing and adoption introduce mid-epoch membership changes, un-deferring the q67.38 obligation: a materializer whose assignment is withdrawn must learn IN-BAND, not wait for the next recovery push. Today the only trigger is {:tsl_updated, ...} (broadcast solely on recovery completion and late-subscriber replay — nothing pushes it mid-epoch), so retirement latency is unbounded, and two live comments already promise in-band behavior that does not exist (distributor/server.ex publish/verification path; recruitment.ex adopt docstring).

MECHANISM (FDB privatization, verified against ../foundationdb 2026-08-24): ApplyMetadataMutation.cpp:293-317 privatizes a serverKeys mutation by prefixing systemKeys.begin — moving the key outside allKeys so no shard can store it — addresses it to the affected server's tag, and writes it into the same commit's mutation stream; storageserver.actor.cpp:11571-11601 recognizes startsWith(systemKeys.end), interprets it via applyPrivateData, and NEVER reaches splitMutation. Interception, not just routing, is what makes it safe.

BEDROCK SHAPE (depends on bedrock-q67.21.9's key shape):
- PRODUCER: in the commit proxy's apply-then-route step, a committed materializers/<tag>/<worker_id> mutation also emits a privatized copy — <<0xFF,0xFF>> <> the same key — routed with an EXPLICIT tag (the shard's own tag, which is already in the key) rather than through split_mutation_by_shards/2, which raises for keys past all shard boundaries. The seam is add_tagged_mutation_to_logs/4, which already takes the tag as a parameter; everything downstream is free, because Demux slices purely by the SHARD_INDEX the proxy writes and never re-examines a key (mutation_slicer.ex). Ordering is already correct: apply precedes route, so the batch that commits the change carries the notice at the same commit version on the stream the victim is already consuming — the victim retires at exactly the version its assignment ends.
- UNFORGEABLE: ingress validation rejects any committed key >= <<0xFF,0xFF>> and runs BEFORE routing (finalization.ex), so only the proxy can synthesize a privatized key.
- CONSUMER: recognize private keys at the materializer's server/ingest boundary, before Logic.apply_transactions — IndexUpdate.apply_mutation/3 has NO filter and would otherwise write the key verbatim into the shard's store (a durable out-of-bounds key that survives compaction and snapshot upload, and corrupts the n_keys/size_in_bytes facts gating idle spin-down). Keeping the recognizer at the boundary also avoids changing IndexManager.apply_transactions/3's contract, which has no channel for a side-effect verdict.
- PREDICATE (collapsed by q67.21.9): a CLEAR of my own key retires me — the worker_id is in the key, so the question is FDB's own "is this about me?" (applyPrivateData's startsWith(data->sk)), not "does this value name me". Multi-instance safe: another worker's key appearing or vanishing is not my business. Replay-safe: worker ids are fresh per recruit, so a replaying instance encounters only other workers' clears; a resurrected worker replaying its own clear and retiring is correct.
- ACTION: reuse the existing displacement path verbatim — Foreman.worker_retired/2 then {:stop, {:shutdown, :displaced}, t}.
- NO EPOCH GATE: validation_due?/2 exists to defend against stale PUSHES. A private mutation on the stream is from the current epoch by construction (the emitting proxy is the current epoch's), so porting the guard would violate the guard-only-real-hazards convention.

Test seam: displacement_test.exs already drives the {:tsl_updated, ...} verdicts through Server.handle_info/2; the in-band pins mirror it against the ingest path.

Do not build before bedrock-q67.21.9 lands: on the single-valued family the predicate would have to be "the entry doesn't name me", which enforces one-materializer-per-shard in the data plane.
title: In-band retirement: the victim learns from its own stream
